doc.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Favorite arrangers and the value of lyrics
summary: Praise for Johnny Mandel and Robert Farnon, and Rodgers and Schwartz and Dietz lyrics.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: No but if you want to hear great arrangements, listen to anything Johnny Mandel wrote or Robert Farnon who was the daddy of all the arrangers. He’s got some great albums, Schwartz and Dietz songs, made in England, unbelievable orchestrations.
A recent Joe Williams record he did.
Oh yeah that’s right, he did Joe’s last album. But I mean he did an instrumental and then you hear the melody with either violin or trombone or maybe electric guitar playing like

George Shearing and his little ensemble with vibes, but what’s going on behind them is unbelievable. All correct. All correct. And then if you’re an English literature major, buy a book on Richard Rogers’ songs and it’s all in there.
All the words. Without the music.
I guess that’s mark of a great lyric. If you take the music away you still have a —
Of course. Schwartz and Dietz, all those songs, “I guess I’ll have to change my plan” and all that stuff. It makes a lot of sense.
